simple.meaning: חָרִישׁ (chârîysh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “ploughing or its season.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Genesis, Exodus, 1 Samuel, beginning at Genesis 45:6. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָרִישׁ (H2758) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָרִישׁ (chârîysh) / H2758 is traced through Genesis 45:6, Exodus 34:21, 1 Samuel 8:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.

timeline.evidenceText: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.
“Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest: in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
